accuracy: The shipped matrix reproduces astropy's own transformation to 2.3e-13 kpc for 20,000 points out to 300 kpc. R0 = 8.122 kpc is GRAVITY 2018, the value the pinned astropy cites; other pinned sources use other values: the Reid+2019 arms were fitted with R0 = 8.15 kpc and the Drimmel+2024 arms appear to use about 8.28 kpc (SpiralMap's default Rsun is 8.277 kpc); both are placed with their own Galactocentric radii.
adaptations: Every galaxy layer is converted into this frame at build time; the 4x4 matrix to ICRS is computed with astropy from transformed points and shipped in galaxy.json.

accuracy: Recomputing each object's Galactocentric distance reproduces LVDB's own distance_gc to 8.7 pc at most (median 2.7 pc, 259 objects), so LVDB used the same frame. Distances equal 10^(DM/5 + 1) pc to 0.15 %; the shipped distance errors come from the catalogued distance-modulus errors (LVDB leaves the kpc errors of the Harris clusters at 0). verify_galaxy.py cross-checks the cluster distances against galpy 1.12.0.
adaptations: 194 Milky Way globular clusters (gc_harris 155 + gc_mw_new 39 with confirmed_real = 1) and 65 satellites (dwarf_mw with confirmed_real = 1, including the LMC and SMC: LVDB confirms 54 as galaxies, and the other 11 could still be star clusters) converted from RA, Dec and distance to Galactocentric kpc. Left out: the 19 unconfirmed cluster candidates, the 22 systems LVDB classes as ambiguous (cluster or dwarf), and 3 unconfirmed dwarfs. Distance, half-light radius (LVDB rhalf_physical, major axis), ellipticity, position angle, M_V and the distance reference are shipped as catalogued.

accuracy: These are smoothed tracks fitted to member stars by each paper, not the stars. Stream widths (typically a fraction of a degree) are not drawn.
adaptations: 100 of the 141 default tracks. Dropped: the 41 Ibata et al. 2024 tracks whose distance is 1.000 kpc everywhere - a placeholder, not a measurement. Kept but marked approximate: 39 tracks with one published distance for the whole track, 9 whose distance varies but is not a measured track (interpolated between published end-point distances, one mean Galactocentric distance, an orbit prediction, or reciprocal parallaxes galstreams flags "with caution"), and the 23 tracks whose sky path is a great circle by construction (InfoFlags bit 0 = 0; they overlap the others). 52 tracks have both a traced path and a measured distance track. Each track decimated to at most 120 evenly indexed points (11,940 in all) and converted to Galactocentric kpc; each carries a note saying what is approximate about it.
owner: Cecilia Mateu (Mateu 2023, MNRAS 520, 5225) and the authors of each track, named per stream

accuracy: A fit, labelled as one. The sign of y was checked at build time against the Reid et al. 2014 maser parallaxes (galkin; not shipped): median |R - R_fit| Local 0.20 kpc (n=25), Perseus 0.23 kpc (n=24), Sgr-Car 0.23 kpc (n=18), Sct-Cen 0.32 kpc (n=17); the mirrored convention gives 0.79, 0.80, 1.23, 1.08 kpc. Fitted with R0 = 8.15 kpc, drawn in a frame with 8.122 kpc.
adaptations: Seven kinked log-spirals R = R_kink exp(-(beta - beta_kink) tan psi) sampled every 1 deg only over each arm's fitted beta range, x = -R cos beta, y = +R sin beta, z = 0; the table's arm widths are shipped as they are.

accuracy: A fit, labelled as one. It disagrees with the maser fit: at the Sun's azimuth the Orion arm lies at R = 9.46 kpc, the Reid Local arm at 8.53 kpc (+0.93 kpc). The fits appear to assume R0 near 8.28 kpc: SpiralMap's default Rsun is 8.277, and in this frame the young Cepheids of Skowron et al. 2019 peak about ln(8.122/8.277) = -0.019 in ln R inside the Scutum and Sagittarius-Carina fits (verify_galaxy.py; Perseus -0.055, Orion shows no clear peak).
adaptations: Variant '1' of the nine azimuth-range fits in the file (phi -90 to 0 deg, 1,331 Cepheids) - the one SpiralMap draws and labels its best phi range, and one of the two variants that fit all four arms. Pitch angle and ln R0 are the mean of the "strength" and "prom" estimates, as SpiralMap does; ln R = ln R0 - tan(pitch) phi, x = -R cos phi, y = R sin phi, sampled every 1 deg only over the fitted range. The paper itself could not be read from the build network, so which variant it calls primary was not checked there.

accuracy: Kernel-smoothed overdensity maps, not star lists. Coverage falls off beyond about 4 kpc (cells with data at 4-5 kpc: gaiadr3_ob 49%, poggio2021_ums 55%). The Gaia DR3 map is clipped at 1.30 by its producers. 8-bit storage: +-0.005.
adaptations: Each 121 x 121 grid (0.1 kpc cells, 6 kpc around the Sun) written as an RGBA PNG at its native resolution: overdensity encoded linearly (-1 to 1.5 -> 0-255) in R = G = B, alpha 0 on the cells that hold exactly 0.0 (no data). Placed around the Sun in the Galactocentric frame; orientation checked against young open clusters (UCC, build-time only).
